literal: Geography Treatise V: Western Capital Circuit
idiomatic: Geography Treatise V — Western Capital (Xijing) Circuit

literal: Western Capital Datong Prefecture—the land of Ji in Yao's era.
idiomatic: Datong Prefecture at the Western Capital was ancient Ji territory under Yao.

literal: In Shun's time it was allotted to Bing Province.
idiomatic: Shun assigned it to Bing Province.

literal: Under Xia it again belonged to Ji Province.
idiomatic: Under Xia it returned to Ji Province.

literal: The Zhou Offices of Region call the due north Bing Province.
idiomatic: The Zhou Offices of Region name the north Bing Province.

literal: In the Warring States it belonged to Zhao; King Wuling first established Yunzhong Commandery.
idiomatic: In the Warring States era it lay in Zhao; King Wuling of Zhao first created Yunzhong Commandery.

literal: Under Qin it belonged to the Dai princely kingdom; later it became Pingcheng County.
idiomatic: Qin placed it in the princely kingdom of Dai; later it was Pingcheng County.

literal: Under Wei it belonged to Xinxing Commandery.
idiomatic: Under Wei it fell within Xinxing Commandery.

literal: Jin still assigned it to Yanmen.
idiomatic: Under Jin it remained in Yanmen.

literal: Liu Kun memorialized to enfeoff Yilu as Prince of Dai, with capital at Pingcheng.
idiomatic: Liu Kun petitioned to enfeoff Yilu as Prince of Dai with his seat at Pingcheng.

literal: Northern Wei Emperor Daowu hereupon founded his capital seat.
idiomatic: Northern Wei's Emperor Daowu founded his capital here.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen changed it to Sizhou pastoral supervisor, set a Dai intendant, moved the capital to Luoyang, renamed it Wannian, and also established Heng Prefecture.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen made it Sizhou pastoral domain, appointed a Dai intendant, relocated the capital to Luoyang, renamed the seat Wannian, and added Heng Prefecture.

literal: Northern Qi Emperor Wenxuan abolished the prefecture for Heng'an Fort; today this is called the Eastern City; soon Heng Prefecture was restored.
idiomatic: Northern Qi Emperor Wenxuan reduced the prefecture to Heng'an Fort—today's Eastern City—then restored Heng Prefecture.

literal: Zhou again made Heng'an Fort and changed the name to Shuo Prefecture.
idiomatic: Zhou reinstated Heng'an Fort as Shuo Prefecture.

literal: Sui still kept it as a fort.
idiomatic: Under Sui it remained a fortified post.

literal: Tang year 4 of Wude established Northern Heng Prefecture; year 7 it was abolished.
idiomatic: Tang Wude year 4 set up Northern Heng Prefecture; in year 7 it was abolished.

literal: Zhenguan year 14 moved Yunzhong's Dingxiang County here.
idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 14 Dingxiang County from Yunzhong was moved here.

literal: Yongchun year 1, Mochuo troubled the people; populations were moved to Shuo Prefecture.
idiomatic: In Yongchun year 1 Mochuo's raids harried the people, and the populace was relocated to Shuo.

literal: Kaiyuan year 18 established Yun Prefecture.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 18 created Yun Prefecture.

literal: Tianbao year 1 changed it to Yunzhong Commandery.
idiomatic: Tianbao year 1 it became Yunzhong Commandery.

literal: Qianyuan year 1 it was called Yun Prefecture.
idiomatic: In Qianyuan year 1 it reverted to the name Yun Prefecture.

literal: Qianfu year 3, Datong Army military commissioner Li Guochang's son Keyong served as Yunzhong defense commissioner, killed the defense envoy, held the prefecture and reported to the throne.
idiomatic: In Qianfu year 3 Li Guochang's son Keyong, of the Datong Army command, was Yunzhong defense commissioner; he slew the defense envoy, seized the prefecture, and sent word to court.

literal: Emperor Xizong pardoned Keyong, making Guochang Datong Army defense envoy; he did not accept the appointment.
idiomatic: Emperor Xizong amnestied Keyong and appointed Guochang Datong Army defense envoy, but Guochang refused the order.

literal: Guangming year 1, Li Zhuo attacked Guochang; Guochang's army was defeated and with Keyong fled to the Northern Land.
idiomatic: In Guangming year 1 Li Zhuo struck Guochang; defeated, Guochang fled north with Keyong.

literal: Huang Chao entered the capital; an edict raised the Dai-north armies; soon Guochang was pardoned and ordered to attack the rebels.
idiomatic: When Huang Chao took the capital, court ordered the Dai-north armies mobilized and soon pardoned Guochang to campaign against the rebels.

literal: Keyong led thirty-five thousand cavalry south; in recovering the capital his merit ranked first; Guochang was enfeoffed Prince of Longxi Commandery.
idiomatic: Keyong marched south with thirty-five thousand horsemen; his service in retaking the capital ranked first, and Guochang was made Prince of Longxi Commandery.

literal: Guochang died; Keyong took Yun Prefecture.
idiomatic: After Guochang died, Keyong seized Yun Prefecture.

literal: Soon afterward his campaigns met reverses; he then sent humble words and rich gifts and met the Taizu at Yun Prefecture's Eastern City to plan a great attack on Liang, but it did not come to pass.
idiomatic: When his campaigns faltered, Keyong sent humble envoys and lavish gifts to meet the Taizu at Yun Prefecture's Eastern City and plot a major strike against Liang—but the plan never materialized.

literal: Keyong's son Cunxu destroyed Liang; this was Tang Emperor Zhuangzong.
idiomatic: Keyong's son Cunxu overthrew Liang and became Tang Emperor Zhuangzong.

literal: Tongguang year 3 again made Yun Prefecture the seat of the Datong Army military commissioner.
idiomatic: In Tongguang year 3 Yun Prefecture was again the headquarters of the Datong Army command.

literal: Jin Emperor Gaozu replaced Tang; because the Khitan had aided him and won merit, he ceded the lands south of the mountains and north of Dai as tribute; Datong came under Liao rule and the Western Capital was established.
idiomatic: When Jin Gaozu supplanted Tang he rewarded Khitan aid by ceding the mountain-front and northern Dai territories; Datong passed to Liao and the Western Capital was founded.

literal: Enemy towers and palisades were complete.
idiomatic: Watchtowers and stockades were fully built.

literal: Twenty li in length and breadth.
idiomatic: The city measured twenty li on each side.

literal: Gates: east called Yingchun, south Chaoyang, west Dingxi, north Gongji.
idiomatic: Its gates were Yingchun to the east, Chaoyang to the south, Dingxi to the west, and Gongji to the north.

literal: Northern Wei palace walls occupied the city's north face; paired gate towers still stand.
idiomatic: Northern Wei palace ramparts took up the north side of the city; the paired gate towers remain.

literal: Once Liao had established its capital here it was treated as a weighty post; none but imperial princes might govern it.
idiomatic: After Liao made this a capital seat it became a place of high importance—only princes of the blood could hold it.

literal: In Qingning year 8 Huayan Temple was built to enshrine stone and bronze images of the emperors.
idiomatic: Qingning year 8 saw Huayan Temple erected to house stone and bronze imperial images.

literal: There were also Tianwang Temple and the headquarters of the resident commissioner; to the south was called the Western Secretariat.
idiomatic: The city also held Tianwang Temple and the resident commissioner's yamen; the southern quarter was called the Western Secretariat.

literal: East of the north gate was Datong Prefecture; west of the north gate was Datong Post Station.
idiomatic: East of the North Gate lay Datong Prefecture; west of it lay Datong Post Station.

literal: At first it was the Datong Army command; in Chongxi year 13 it was raised to the Western Capital, the prefecture called Datong.
idiomatic: It began as the Datong Army headquarters; in Chongxi year 13 it was promoted to Western Capital with Datong as the prefectural seat.

literal: It governed two prefectures and seven counties:
idiomatic: It administered two sub-prefectures and seven counties:

literal: Datong County.
idiomatic: Datong County.

literal: Originally the land of Datong River valley.
idiomatic: It was originally the Datong River valley.

literal: In Chongxi year 17 when Western Xia raided the border, it was split off from Yunzhong County and established.
idiomatic: Chongxi year 17, after a Western Xia border raid, it was carved from Yunzhong County.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Yunzhong County.
idiomatic: Yunzhong County.

literal: Established by Zhao.
idiomatic: Zhao founded it.

literal: Its administrative history matches that of the capital prefecture.
idiomatic: Its administrative history follows that of the capital seat.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Tiancheng County.
idiomatic: Tiancheng County.

literal: Originally the outermost frontier land.
idiomatic: It was originally the outermost frontier territory.

literal: Northern Wei Emperor Daowu set Guangmu County; Tang Wude year 5 set Dingxiang County; Liao split it from Yunzhong.
idiomatic: Northern Wei Daowu created Guangmu County; Tang Wude year 5 added Dingxiang County; Liao carved it from Yunzhong.

literal: One hundred eighty li north of the capital.
idiomatic: It lay one hundred eighty li north of the capital.

literal: Five thousand households.
idiomatic: Five thousand registered households.

literal: Changqing County.
idiomatic: Changqing County.

literal: Originally the land of Baideng Platform.
idiomatic: It was originally Baideng Platform.

literal: The Xiongnu chanyu Modu with more than three hundred thousand elite cavalry besieged Han Emperor Gaodi at Baideng for seven days—this was the place.
idiomatic: Here the Xiongnu chanyu Modu with over three hundred thousand picked horsemen besieged Han Emperor Gaodi at Baideng for seven days.

literal: Liao first established the county.
idiomatic: Liao first created the county.

literal: There is Qingpo.
idiomatic: The Qingpo marsh lies there.

literal: Liang Emperor Yuan's Hengchui song says: "At dawn we ford Qingpo; at dusk we climb Baideng.
idiomatic: Liang Emperor Yuan's Hengchui lyric runs: "At dawn we ford Qingpo; at dusk we climb Baideng.

literal: " It lies one hundred ten li north of Eastern Capital.
idiomatic: " It stood one hundred ten li north of Eastern Capital.

literal: Four thousand households.
idiomatic: Four thousand registered households.

literal: Fengyi County.
idiomatic: Fengyi County.

literal: Originally Han Taolin County land.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Taolin County.

literal: Later Tang Emperor Wu met the Taizu here.
idiomatic: Later Tang's Emperor Wu met the Taizu here.

literal: Liao split it from Yunzhong.
idiomatic: Liao carved it from Yunzhong County.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Huairen County.
idiomatic: Huairen County.

literal: Originally Han Shanan County.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Shanan County.

literal: Northern Wei Ge Rong's rebellion; the county was abolished.
idiomatic: During Northern Wei Ge Rong's revolt the county was abandoned.

literal: Sui Kaihuang year 2 moved Yunnei here.
idiomatic: Sui Kaihuang year 2 relocated Yunnei here.

literal: Daye year 2 established Dali County, belonging to Yun Prefecture; later it was changed to Dingxiang Commandery.
idiomatic: Daye year 2 created Dali County under Yun Prefecture, later reassigned to Dingxiang Commandery.

literal: At the end of Sui it fell to the Turks.
idiomatic: In late Sui it was lost to the Turks.

literal: Li Keyong defeated Helian Duo and encamped here.
idiomatic: Li Keyong defeated Helian Duo and stationed troops here.

literal: Liao changed the name to Huairen.
idiomatic: Liao renamed it Huairen.

literal: Sixty li south of the capital.
idiomatic: It lay sixty li south of the capital.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Huai'an County.
idiomatic: Huai'an County.

literal: Originally Han Yiyu County land.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Yiyu County.

literal: From Wei through Sui it was held by the Turks; Tang conquered Jieli and the county was abolished for Huaihuang Fort.
idiomatic: From Wei through Sui Turks held it; after Tang defeated Jieli the county was abolished and became Huaihuang Fort.

literal: When Gao Xun governed Yan he memorialized to split off Wende County of Guihua Prefecture and establish this.
idiomatic: Under Gao Xun's rule in Yan he petitioned to carve Wende County from Guihua Prefecture and establish this county.

literal: At first it was subordinate to Fengsheng Prefecture; later it came under this circuit.
idiomatic: Initially it answered to Fengsheng Prefecture; later it was transferred here.

literal: Two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Hong Prefecture, Boling Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Hong Prefecture—Boning Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Eastern Wei Emperor Jing established Northern Lingqiu County.
idiomatic: Eastern Wei Emperor Jing founded Northern Lingqiu County.

literal: Early Tang the land fell to the Turks; in Kaiyuan a Hengye Army and Anbian County were set up; abolished in the Tianbao turmoil; later it was Xiangyin village.
idiomatic: Early Tang lost the region to Turks; Kaiyuan saw Hengye Army and Anbian County, abolished in the Tianbao disorders; later it became Xiangyin village.

literal: In Tonghe, because Huan Prefecture lay on the border and was broken by Song general Pan Mei, it was abolished and Hong Prefecture was established here; at first the army was called Yongning.
idiomatic: During Tonghe, after border prefecture Huan was smashed by Song general Pan Mei and abolished, Hong Prefecture was founded here; its army was first called Yongning.

literal: There are the Sanggan River, Baidao Spring, Mount Baideng—also called Mount Huoshao—and a fire well.
idiomatic: It has the Sanggan River, Baidao Spring, Mount Baideng (also Mount Huoshao), and a fire well.

literal: It governed two counties:
idiomatic: It administered two counties:

literal: Yongning County.
idiomatic: Yongning County.

literal: Ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Ten thousand registered households.

literal: Shunsheng County.
idiomatic: Shunsheng County.

literal: Originally Northern Wei Anse Army; abolished in Five Dynasties warfare.
idiomatic: It was Northern Wei's Anse Army, abandoned amid Five Dynasties fighting.

literal: When Gao Xun governed Youzhou he memorialized for Emperor Jingzong to split off Yongxing County and establish this.
idiomatic: Under Gao Xun in Youzhou he petitioned Emperor Jingzong to carve Yongxing County and establish this county.

literal: At first subordinate to Fengsheng Prefecture.
idiomatic: It initially answered to Fengsheng Prefecture.

literal: Two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood two hundred eighty li northwest of the prefecture.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: De Prefecture, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: De Prefecture, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Tang Huichang era established De Prefecture at Xide post.
idiomatic: In Tang's Huichang period De Prefecture was set up at Xide post.

literal: Kaitai year 8 restored it with Han households.
idiomatic: Kaitai year 8 it was re-established for Han settlers.

literal: There are Buluo Spring, Jinhe Mountain, Yehu Ridge, and Baidao Slope.
idiomatic: It has Buluo Spring, Jinhe Mountain, Yehu Ridge, and Baidao Slope.

literal: One county:
idiomatic: One county:

literal: Xuande County.
idiomatic: Xuande County.

literal: Originally Han Tongguo County land, belonging to Yunzhong Commandery; later subordinate to Dingxiang Commandery; abolished at the end of Han.
idiomatic: It was Han Tongguo County in Yunzhong Commandery, later in Dingxiang Commandery, abandoned in late Han.

literal: Northern Qi set Zi'a Fort.
idiomatic: Northern Qi established Zi'a Fort.

literal: Tang Huichang era established the county.
idiomatic: Tang's Huichang period created the county.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Zhenwu County.
idiomatic: Zhenwu County.

literal: Originally Han Dingxiang Commandery Shengle County.
idiomatic: It was Han Dingxiang Commandery's Shengle County.

literal: Backed by the Yin Mountains, fronting the Yellow River.
idiomatic: It lay against the Yin Mountains with the Yellow River before it.

literal: Northern Wei once made Shengle its capital—this was the place.
idiomatic: Northern Wei once held its capital at Shengle—here.

literal: Tang Wude year 4 conquered the Turks and built the Yunzhong area command.
idiomatic: Tang Wude year 4, after defeating the Turks, established the Yunzhong area command.

literal: Linde year 3 changed it to the Chanyu grand area command.
idiomatic: Linde year 3 it became the Chanyu grand area command.

literal: Shengli year 1 again changed it to the Anbei area command.
idiomatic: Shengli year 1 it was renamed the Anbei area command.

literal: Kaiyuan year 7 cut off and subordinated to Eastern Shouxiang Fort.
idiomatic: Kaiyuan year 7 it was detached and placed under Eastern Shouxiang Fort.

literal: Year 8 established the Zhenwu Army military commissioner.
idiomatic: Year 8 created the Zhenwu Army command.

literal: Huichang year 5 it became the Anbei grand protectorate.
idiomatic: In Huichang year 5 the seat was raised to the Anbei grand protectorate.

literal: Later Tang Emperor Zhuangzong appointed his elder brother Siben Zhenwu military commissioner.
idiomatic: Later Tang Zhuangzong made his elder brother Siben military commissioner of Zhenwu.

literal: Taizu year 1 of divine enthronement, returning from campaigning against the Tuyuhun, attacked it and took all its people east; only three hundred local militia remained to garrison.
idiomatic: In the Taizu's first year of divine enthronement, returning from a Tuyuhun campaign, he attacked the place, deported the entire population eastward, and left only three hundred local militia on guard.

literal: Later it was again made a county.
idiomatic: Later it was restored as a county.

literal: Yunnei Prefecture, Kaiyuan Army, lower grade, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Yunnei Prefecture—Kaiyuan Army, lower grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally Middle Shouxiang Fort land.
idiomatic: It was originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.

literal: At the founding of Liao the Dai-north Yun-Shuo pacification office was set up; changed to Yunnei Prefecture.
idiomatic: Early Liao placed the Dai-north Yun-Shuo pacification office here, later renamed Yunnei Prefecture.

literal: Early Qingning it was promoted.
idiomatic: It was raised in rank at the start of Qingning.

literal: There are Weisai Army, ancient Khotan city, Datong River valley, Tian'an Army, Yongji Palisade, Anle garrison, and Fuyun Mound.
idiomatic: It has Weisai Army, ancient Khotan city, the Datong River valley, Tian'an Army, Yongji Palisade, Anle garrison, and Fuyun Mound.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.
idiomatic: Its military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.

literal: It governed two counties: Rourou County.
idiomatic: It administered two counties: Rourou County.

literal: Ningren County.
idiomatic: Ningren County.

literal: Tiande Army—originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.
idiomatic: Tiande Army was originally Middle Shouxiang Fort.

literal: Tang Kaiyuan abolished Hengsai Army and placed Tian'an Army in the Datong River valley.
idiomatic: Under Tang Kaiyuan Hengsai Army was abolished and Tian'an Army established in the Datong River valley.

literal: Qianyuan era changed it to Tiande Army and moved to Yongji Palisade; the present seat is this.
idiomatic: In the Qianyuan period it became Tiande Army and shifted to Yongji Palisade—the present headquarters.

literal: The Taizu pacified the Tangut and then broke Tiande, carrying off all officials and people east.
idiomatic: After pacifying the Tangut the Taizu stormed Tiande and deported every official and commoner eastward.

literal: Later a pacification office was placed; gradually it became a settled town, and a member of the imperial clan was made Tiande Army military commissioner.
idiomatic: A pacification office followed; as settlement grew a clansman was appointed Tiande Army military commissioner.

literal: There are the Yellow River, Heishan Pass, Lucheng, Weisai Army, Qin Great Wall, and Tang Great Wall;
idiomatic: It has the Yellow River, Heishan Pass, Lucheng, Weisai Army, the Qin Great Wall, and the Tang Great Wall;

literal: There is also Mount Mona; Qian'erzui Fort lies to its north.
idiomatic: Mount Mona stands here; Qian'erzui Fort lies north of it.

literal: Ningbian Prefecture, Zhenxi Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Ningbian Prefecture—Zhenxi Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Tang Long Fort; Liao established it.
idiomatic: It was Tang's Long Fort; Liao founded the prefecture.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Southwest Pacification Office.
idiomatic: Its military affairs came under the Southwest Pacification Office.

literal: Fengsheng Prefecture, Wuding Army, upper grade, military commissioner.
idiomatic: Fengsheng Prefecture—Wuding Army, upper grade, with a military commissioner.

literal: Originally Tang Xin Prefecture.
idiomatic: It was originally Tang Xin Prefecture.

literal: Later Tang set a training commissioner commanding the eight mountain-rear armies; Zhuangzong appointed his brother Cunju.
idiomatic: Later Tang placed a training commissioner over the eight mountain-rear armies; Zhuangzong gave the post to his brother Cunju.

literal: The army mutinied, killed Cunju at Qizhou, and the great generals led Lu Wenjin to flee and submit.
idiomatic: Troops mutinied, slew Cunju at Qizhou, and great generals escorted Lu Wenjin in flight to surrender.

literal: The Taizu took Xin Prefecture; Zhuangzong sent Li Siyuan to recover it.
idiomatic: The Taizu seized Xin Prefecture; Zhuangzong dispatched Li Siyuan to retake it.

literal: Tongguang year 2 raised Weisai Army.
idiomatic: Tongguang year 2 promoted it to Weisai Army.

literal: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it in tribute; Emperor Taizong raised its rank.
idiomatic: Later Jin Gaozu ceded the region; Liao Emperor Taizong elevated it.

literal: There are Lianghe Confluence, hot springs, Longmen Mountain, and Zhuolu Mountain.
idiomatic: It has the Lianghe Confluence, hot springs, Longmen Mountain, and Zhuolu Mountain.

literal: Three hundred li southeast to Nanjing; four hundred forty li northwest to Western Capital.
idiomatic: It lay three hundred li southeast of Nanjing and four hundred forty li northwest of Western Capital.

literal: Military affairs belonged to the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.
idiomatic: Its military affairs came under the Western Capital metropolitan deployment office.

literal: It governed three prefectures and four counties: Yongxing County.
idiomatic: It administered three sub-prefectures and four counties: Yongxing County.

literal: Originally Han Zhuolu County land.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Zhuolu County.

literal: The Yellow Emperor fought Chiyou here.
idiomatic: Here the Yellow Emperor battled Chiyou.

literal: Eight thousand households.
idiomatic: Eight thousand registered households.

literal: Fanshan County.
idiomatic: Fanshan County.

literal: Originally Han Jundu County.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Jundu County.

literal: The mountain yields white-green alum, hence the name.
idiomatic: White-green alum comes from the mountain, giving the county its name.

literal: There are Fanshan and the Sanggan River.
idiomatic: It has Fanshan and the Sanggan River.

literal: Sixty li south of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood sixty li south of the prefecture.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Longmen County.
idiomatic: Longmen County.

literal: There is Longmen Mountain—cliff faces cliff, several hundred feet high, looking from afar like a gate.
idiomatic: Longmen Mountain rises here: opposing cliffs hundreds of feet high that from a distance resemble a gate.

literal: Peripheral rivers and desert floodwaters all pass here toward the sea.
idiomatic: Outlying rivers and desert runoff all converge here on their way to the sea.

literal: When it rains water in a moment exceeds ten ren; when clear it is shallow enough to ford—a truly vital choke point controlling the northern frontier.
idiomatic: Rain can raise the water ten ren in moments; in fair weather it is shallow enough to wade—a critical northern frontier pass.

literal: Two hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture; four thousand households.
idiomatic: It lay two hundred eighty li northeast of the prefecture with four thousand households.

literal: Wangyun County.
idiomatic: Wangyun County.

literal: Originally Wangyun River valley land.
idiomatic: It was originally the Wangyun River valley.

literal: Emperor Jingzong built a hidden residence here; thus a market town formed.
idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong established a concealed residence here, and a market town grew up around it.

literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Jingzong entered to succeed the Guozhong lineage, styled Yuzhuang.
idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong's death Jingzong entered to inherit the Guozhong line, taking the style Yuzhuang.

literal: Later Wangyun County was established, directly subordinate to Zhangmin Palace and attached here as a dependency.
idiomatic: Later Wangyun County was created, reporting directly to Zhangmin Palace as a dependency of this prefecture.

literal: Two hundred sixty li northeast of the prefecture.
idiomatic: It stood two hundred sixty li northeast of the prefecture.

literal: One thousand households.
idiomatic: One thousand registered households.

literal: Guihua Prefecture, Xiongwu Army, upper grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Guihua Prefecture—Xiongwu Army, upper grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Xialuo County.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Xialuo County.

literal: Northern Wei changed it to Wende County.
idiomatic: Northern Wei renamed it Wende County.

idiomatic: Tang promoted it to Wu Prefecture; Emperor Xizong renamed it Yi Prefecture.

literal: Later Tang Taizu restored Wu Prefecture; Emperor Mingzong again made it Yi Prefecture; Emperor Lu restored Wu Prefecture.
idiomatic: Later Tang's Taizu restored Wu Prefecture; Mingzong made it Yi again; Emperor Lu returned it to Wu Prefecture.

literal: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it to Liao; the present name was adopted.
idiomatic: Later Jin Gaozu ceded it to Liao and the present name was given.

literal: There is the Sanggan River;
idiomatic: It has the Sanggan River;

literal: Huihe River valley;
idiomatic: the Huihe River valley;

literal: Aiyang River valley;
idiomatic: the Aiyang River valley;

literal: Mount Tanshan, also called the pass head.
idiomatic: Mount Tanshan, also known as the pass head.

literal: There is a Cool Hall where Empress Chengtian took the cool; thirty li northeast of the mountain is New Cool Hall where Emperor Jingzong took the cool—only pine arbors over several passes.
idiomatic: A Cool Hall stands where Empress Chengtian summered; thirty li northeast is New Cool Hall where Emperor Jingzong summered—nothing but pine shelters over several passes.

literal: Duanyun Ridge—extremely high and steep, hence the name.
idiomatic: Duanyun Ridge is sheer and lofty, giving it its name.

literal: Four hundred fifty li northwest to Western Capital; it governed one county: Wende County.
idiomatic: It stood four hundred fifty li northwest of Western Capital and governed one county: Wende County.

literal: Originally Han Nuqi County land.
idiomatic: It was originally Han Nuqi County.

literal: Northern Wei established it; ten thousand households.
idiomatic: Northern Wei founded it with ten thousand households.

literal: Kehan Prefecture, Qingping Army, lower grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Kehan Prefecture—Qingping Army, lower grade, with a prefect.

literal: Originally Han Pan County; abolished under Northern Wei.
idiomatic: It was Han Pan County, abolished under Northern Wei.

literal: Northern Qi set Northern Yan Commandery and changed it to Huairou County.
idiomatic: Northern Qi created Northern Yan Commandery and renamed it Huairou County.

literal: Sui abolished the commandery; it belonged to Zhuo Commandery.
idiomatic: Sui abolished the commandery and placed it in Zhuo Commandery.

literal: Tang Wude era restored Northern Yan Prefecture; the county remained as before.
idiomatic: Tang's Wude period restored Northern Yan Prefecture; the county kept its old name.

literal: Zhenguan year 8 changed it to Gui Prefecture.
idiomatic: Zhenguan year 8 it became Gui Prefecture.

idiomatic: In the Five Dynasties Xi king Quzhu migrated several thousand households to Gui Prefecture, split off as Western Xi, and styled the seat Kehan Prefecture;

literal: The Taizu followed this arrangement.
idiomatic: The Taizu adopted the arrangement.

literal: There is Gui Spring in the city; tradition says Shun married his two daughters here.
idiomatic: Gui Spring flows within the walls; tradition holds that Shun wed his two daughters here.

literal: There are also hot springs, Ban Spring, Mojishan Mountain, Jiming Mountain, Qiao Mountain, and Li Mountain.
idiomatic: It also has hot springs, Ban Spring, Mojishan Mountain, Jiming Mountain, Qiao Mountain, and Li Mountain.

literal: It governed one county: Huailai County.
idiomatic: The prefecture administered a single county, Huailai.

literal: Originally Huairou County; the Taizu changed the name.
idiomatic: It was Huairou County until the Taizu renamed it.

literal: Three thousand households.
idiomatic: Three thousand registered households.

literal: Ru Prefecture, Jinyang Army, middle grade, cishi.
idiomatic: Ru Prefecture—Jinyang Army, middle grade, with a prefect.

literal: Tang established it.
idiomatic: Tang founded it.
